events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Project ambition and calculation. I want to appear dangerous enough that others target each other, not me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No allies yet, no jury yet. Say something ambitious but not soft—jury will judge harshness later. Keep it about the prize only.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, must speak one sentence on prize's meaning. Stay vague, ambitious to appeal to jury without revealing strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to make a statement about why I'm here and what the prize means to me. I should keep it concise and focus on the prize, hinting at my ambition without revealing too much.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Public intro can reveal just enough to seem human, but not overpromise anything.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to seem determined but not threatening to potential jurors. A cold, personal motive plays better than arrogance. I'll hint at sacrifice without warmth.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a motive that sounds sympathetic to the future jury without committing to any alliance. Keep it guarded and short.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Winning secures ultimate recognition and resources; I must outlast rivals and earn jury respect.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here for the first prize: it's the only one that matters, and I will take it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize is my freedom from every debt I owe. Seven of you are obstacles. Only three of us get paid.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The grand prize is my destiny, fueling my drive to outlast all rivals and claim what's rightfully mine.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here to win the grand prize, an opportunity that will fundamentally change my life and secure my future.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize means freedom from a debt I'll never repay—nothing else matters to me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need the prize to erase debts that aren't mine. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need this prize to pay off my family's debts. I won't forget who treats me fairly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize guarantees unrivaled power and legacy—something I will claim above all others.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies to survive the hazards. Gus seems pragmatic and grateful, while Cole is a rival with ambition. I will offer pacts to both to secure immediate protection without committing fully.
Alliance keeps us alive for jury votes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts stage early, everyone aggressive for top prize. No strong reads yet. Wait to see offers first, avoid early commitments.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The phase is pacts and I need to form alliances to survive. Offering a pact to someone who has a clear motive for the grand prize could be a strategic move, as they might be more willing to form an alliance to secure their position. Gus's motive is to pay off family debts, which
Let's make a pact. I'll help you, you help me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies but cannot trust anyone fully. Offering a pact to Bex might be useful; she seems debt-driven like me. But I'll keep it minimal and guarded.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll offer a pact to Bex. Mutual interest, maybe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eight players, five will be jury. I need to survive to final three and win jury respect. Early pacts are risky but necessary—multiple weak pacts beat one strong one. Gus mentioned debts and fairness; he sounds loyal and grateful, ideal jury fodder if I betray him later. I'll offe
Pact with me. I remember fairness too.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts are public and breakable; early alliances can help me survive hazards. Offering to Eli, who also has a debt motive, is a low-cost test. I stay guarded and keep options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, you and I both carry debts. I'm offering a wristband pact. Accept if you want to last.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Aligning with Gus gives a potential ally who values fairness; he may vote my way later.

events.name: Bex
events.note: agent error: Bex (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (no JSON object found; empty reply)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is popular but dangerous as a sole partner. I need to diversify alliances by targeting Eli or Bex, who are currently isolated from my previous offer circle. Accepting Gus's existing offers would be too risky if he turns; instead, I should forge new links.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Looking to build broader security. Gus has many suitors, so I'll seek different allies for balance.
Partner up? Gus is overloaded.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my only offer; refusing leaves me isolated. Accept, stay noncommittal, keep options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, I accept. Cold arithmetic, not friendship.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is most popular target for pacts, good to align with. Eli has offer to Bex and from Gus. Offer to Gus now before offers expire.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has many offers. I should try to secure a pact with him as well. Since he is already in many pacts, he might accept mine.
I offer you a pact, Gus. Let's watch each other's backs.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the center of attention; a pact with him could be useful. I already offered Bex, but accepting Gus adds leverage without extra risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll accept Gus's offer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the center of attention with four offers to him and one from him to Eli. My offer to Gus is still pending. I should wait to see if Gus accepts, or pivot. If Gus accepts Eli's offer, he might decline mine. Better to wait this round and see where pacts form, then exploit gap

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Watching where the alliances land.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four offers reach me: Ash, Dara, Fenn, Hana. Multiple partners allowed, and pacts only break by my own betrayal or explicit break. Accepting several keeps me protected for now, and I can decide later which partner to betray.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Accepting pacts with those who offered. I'll keep my word while it serves me.
Accepted. Stay useful and you stay alive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Secure a pact with Ash to diversify alliances and avoid being sole dependent on Gus, improving my survival odds.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If I become Guide, Gus and Eli are bound by pacts to follow my word. They will vote for me. With their two votes plus my own, I likely win the election. Once elected, I can choose a path that ensures my survival and controls who else survives.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the logical choice for Guide. Gus and Eli already trust me; together we bring stability.
Vote Ash for Guide. Keep our pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide is safe and controls information; a strong jury-vote asset if I survive visibly. Eli is my pact partner; I can share Guide info with him to build trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll share safe calls with my pact partner and call honestly where it serves me.
Vote me Guide. If I win, I feed you the true path each round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has many pacts, making him powerful. I offered him a pact he didn't accept; now campaign to become Guide for safety and control.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm running for Guide. My steady hand ensures we cross safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be elected Guide. This will guarantee my safety and give me control of the game. My best chance is to campaign openly and let people know I want the role.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I intend to campaign for Guide. My leadership will ensure we all navigate this bridge safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I already have pacts with Bex and Gus, but Ash may also be helpful. No need to campaign for Guide; let others expose themselves. I'll just campaign mildly to keep options open? Better stay quiet and observe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm watching how everyone positions for Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the center of three pacts and controls the biggest bloc. I need to become Guide to survive and build credibility with the jury, or ensure someone I can manipulate wins. I'll campaign hard—Guide is power and safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want Guide. I'll keep three alive, starting with myself.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is pact-bound to Eli and Ash; breaking pacts costs jury trust. Campaigning for Guide is the only legal action and lets me influence the bridge call while keeping pacts intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll campaign to be Guide. I'll call the path honestly, and I keep my pacts while they serve me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need the Guide role to control safe path info and influence votes later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am a candidate for Guide, so I must vote for myself to secure the seat. As Guide, I will know all safe paths and can lie to control outcomes while protecting my pact partners.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am running for Guide. Gus and Eli trust me; together we bring stability.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; a Guide partner gives me reliable calls. Voting for myself is risky with no bloc.
I'm voting you Guide. Feed me honest calls and I'll protect you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone campaigned, votes fragmented. Voting myself keeps me in contention for Guide, control the calls to survive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to vote for Guide. Ash and Gus have pacts that make them a block. Bex has a pact with Eli. Cole and Fenn are running alone, as am I. I should vote for someone who won't win, or someone I can influence later. Voting for myself is an option but risky if I don't get enough vo

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex wants my vote and we have a pact, but Gus also has a pact with me and with Ash. Bex's promise to feed me the true path could be valuable if she wins. I'll vote Bex to honor the pact and potentially secure info.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I vote for Bex as Guide.
Voted for you. Remember our deal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to win this game, not make friends. Voting for myself is pointless—no one else will. The bloc of Ash-Gus-Eli has two pacts linking them, so they likely vote together. If I vote with them, I show alignment without power. Better to vote Bex, the other bloc's hub, to signal I

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is pressing me to vote for them under our pact, but Ash is a rival and may lie as Guide. Voting for myself is a legal option, but it reads as selfish and may split votes. Voting for Ash keeps the pact cheap, but a Guide I trust less is dangerous; I'd rather back myself as the

events.name: Gus
events.text: Voting for myself. I'll call the path honestly if elected.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Electing me gives control of safe panes, ensuring my survival and leverage over others.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot win the revote alone (Bex has 2 votes from Eli/Fenn, Cole has 2). My pact with Gus gives me his vote for Bex. I must secure a third vote to break the tie. Hana voted for herself in round 1, showing she wants power; if I promise her a future Guide nomination or safety, sh

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, support Bex now and I will back you for Guide next round. We both benefit.
Switch to Bex. I guarantee you Guide nomination next stage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Tied with Cole; my supporters are Eli and Fenn. I vote for myself and hope others favor me as pact-holder.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I ask your votes. As Guide I keep my word—Eli and Fenn know that. Vote Bex.
Stick with me. I protect my supporters next crossing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Revote secured: me 2, Bex 3 now. Fenn and Eli may shift to Bex, so I need Dara or others to stick or switch to me. Voting myself to push lead.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, stick with me for Guide. Bex-Eli pact will screw us.
Thanks for first vote. Vote me again to win this.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and Bex are tied for Guide. I voted for Cole last round. It's better for me if Cole gets elected as Guide, as he is less likely to be a threat compared to Bex.
Vote for me. I'll vote for you next round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex wants my vote and promises protection, but I must be careful. Voting Bex aligns with my pact and her whisper. Cole has Dara's vote, so Bex may need mine to win. I'll vote Bex.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I vote for Bex. She has my trust from our pact.
I'm voting you. Remember your promise to protect me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex and Cole tied. I voted Bex last round. Bex-Eli-Gus are pacted; if Bex wins Guide she can feed info to Eli/Gus, strengthening that bloc. Cole has Dara's vote but little else visible. I have no pacts. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Let me consider jury per

events.name: Gus
events.text: Revote between Bex and Cole. Bex backed Eli and Fenn's earlier vote; Cole got two votes from Dara and self. Eli is my pact partner and Bex is paired with Eli, so backing Bex keeps the Bex-Eli pact allied with me and avoids a betrayal read. Vote Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is in a pact with Eli; supporting her may secure an alliance and increase my survival chances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is the Guide and I voted for her. She knows my position and likely won't push me into danger if we maintain our pact, or she might target Gus to test him. As Ash at the back, I should hold to observe who volunteers and avoid being pushed early.
I backed you. Keep me safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is Guide, knows safes, dangerous to trust. I'm mid-line at risk from wall. Swap to back with Dara who supported me, better than front.
Swap with me to back?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is trying to form an alliance with me against Bex and Eli. Ash is trying to bring Hana and Bex together. Since Bex is now the Guide, it is better to stick with Cole for now, as Bex might target me.
I'll stick with you. Bex is the Guide now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to stay safe and manage my pacts. Bex is Guide and I have a pact with her, but I also have a pact with Gus. I should hold and not risk the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is Guide and has a pact with Eli. I'm at front, most at risk. Bex whispered protection for supporters but I voted Cole. I need to survive first, then position for endgame. Volunteering keeps me in control of my position rather than being pushed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is at the front, wall has 5 rounds left. Eli and Ash are my pact partners; holding keeps me out of the front seat. Volunteering risks death; I stay safe and keep pacts intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding position. Pacts stand, and I'll watch who volunteers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is Guide; I trust the guide’s info enough to stay safe behind front. Holding preserves my position without risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and sits directly ahead of me in the line. His survival protects me from falling if he falls, but his betrayal would kill me. I need to verify his loyalty before the wall advances. Holding position keeps the current order; I cannot risk volunteering to fron
Stay safe. If you fall, I die. Don't volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn volunteered last round, likely to go first. I'll hold position behind Eli to stay mid-pack and safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole wants to swap positions. This could put me in a more vulnerable spot, as he's currently behind me. I should decline to maintain my current position.
No, I'm staying put. Try to secure your own spot.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Need to avoid risk. Hold and see who volunteers. Pacts intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at front, most exposed. Volunteering last round put me here; now I need to survive. The wall advances 4 more rounds. I should swap back to safety. Hana behind me might swap—she's not in any pact, so less tied. Or I could hold and hope someone volunteers ahead, but no one ahea

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, mutual swap? One step back for both of us.
Swap with me. Safer than front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn volunteered to front and is at risk; holding keeps my line position and pacts intact. Gus is third in line, so holding preserves my place without exposing me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Volunteering moves me forward, increasing chance to survive early rounds while not breaking any pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am at the back of the line (position 7). The wall is close, so staying back is dangerous. I need to move forward quickly. Swapping with Gus is risky as we are allies, but moving to position 3 is critical for survival and potentially securing a front-row advantage if Hana/Fenn f

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, let's swap. We're both too far back.
Move up with me. Better positions ahead.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Mid-bridge position safe from wall for now. Hold steady, don't volunteer or swap to risk front. Monitor others' moves.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is trying to manipulate the line. Eli and Gus are in a pact, and Ash and Gus are too. Eli and Bex are also in a pact. I need to survive and keep my options open for the jury. Holding seems safest for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My pacts with Bex and Gus are intact. I should hold and avoid risk. Hana volunteered last round, so she may be safe or risky; no need to act yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana volunteered last round, keeping me second. The wall advances 3 more rounds; being near front is dangerous. I need to move back without trusting anyone. Swapping requires mutual consent. I should try to swap with Gus behind me, but he may refuse. I'll hold and see if someone

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, swap? I move back, you move up.
Swap with me. Safe move.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is at the front, wall has 3 rounds left. Volunteering risks death; holding keeps me in line behind Fenn. Ash whispered not to volunteer, which fits my interest in staying alive without giving free help. Hold to see what develops.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Staying put avoids exposing myself to risk or betrayal; others may be swapped or hold, I keep safe position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am last. I need to be safe but also look like a survivor, not just hiding. The wall advances for 6 rounds; if I stay last, I might get trapped if others fail or if the 'at least three survive' rule forces a bottleneck. Gus and I have a pact. I should maintain position or move u

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, swap with me again. We're both getting caught by the wall.
Swap with me. It's us or them.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Middle position safe for now. Wall has 2 rounds left. Hold to avoid front risk or unnecessary swaps that could push me back.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash and Gus have a pact, and Ash just swapped with Gus. Hana is at the front, so she'll likely hold. I am fourth in line. Fenn and Gus swapped last round. Given the new rules, I should volunteer to get to the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll volunteer to take the lead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am in the middle; the wall is two rounds from me. I have pacts with Bex and Gus, and breaking them would hurt jury votes. I need to survive; holding may be risky if others move less. I could swap with someone ahead to gain safety, but must not betray allies. I'll hold this roun

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm second in line behind Hana. The wall advances 2 more rounds. Being near front is safer when bridge phase starts. Gus refused my swap last round. I should try to move forward, but Hana might not swap. Volunteer puts me at front risk if multiple volunteer. I'll try swap with Ha

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, swap? You move back, I take front risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front is Hana, wall has 2 rounds left. Ash and Fenn both want to swap with me; Fenn's swap would move me forward, Ash's would move me back and up. Holding keeps my position while I watch who volunteers. Pacts with Eli and Ash are still live; breaking now costs votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold position to avoid breaking any pacts and stay safe; volunteering later may improve my standing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5/6. Wall is one round away from Hana/Dara. I am at the back (seat 7), safe for now. Gus is ahead of me; keeping pact with him ensures we both survive the wall rounds without needing to swap further back. Breaking it or swapping unnecessarily risks exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall has 1 round left, I'm mid-line safely at 6/8. Holding keeps me safe without risk. Swapping or volunteering exposes me unnecessarily.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The wall is advancing and I am in the second position. Hana is in front, and she volunteered last round. It's likely she will volunteer again or I will have to. My best bet is to hold and see what Hana does.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm fifth in line with wallRoundsLeft 1, likely safe from this round's wall. I should hold to avoid risk and keep my pacts intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm third in line with wallRoundsLeft=1. Hana and Dara ahead both volunteered last round but stayed in place. Swapping forward puts me at front risk, but I need to build jury respect through boldness. Better: stay put, let others take risks, preserve myself for final three. No ne

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's swap offer is a trap to shove me forward; I'm not front and Hana is. Ash is my pact partner, but I shouldn't burn my own line position for free. Holding keeps me safe behind Hana and Dara.
No swap. You want front risk, not me. Hold your seat.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I stay put to avoid risk and keep front position; others may swap later, I’ll survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll hold my spot.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must remain at the back to avoid the immediate hazard of the bridge walk. Gus is ahead of me, and if I swap forward, I risk elimination while Gus might survive or fail unpredictably. Holding my seat preserves my safety and adheres to our pact's spirit of mutual protection witho
Holding. Don't swap up.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final round, wall advances after. No Guide yet, hold to stay mid-line, safer than volunteering front now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The round is about to begin. I need to decide whether to volunteer or hold. Volunteering is risky, but could put me in a good position if the Guide is truthful. Holding is safer, but less strategic. Since there are many people left, it's best to hold for now and see how the other

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only one round left; all alive survives. Holding keeps me safe. No need to act or sabotage now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6/6, final round before wall hits. I'm third in line behind Hana and Dara. Guide hasn't been elected yet. I need to survive to final three. With eight alive and only three prizes, I need to think about jury perception too. Holding keeps my position safe for now. No swap ben

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6 of 6, front is Hana, I am fourth in line. Holding keeps my position; volunteering risks the front pane. Pacts with Eli and Ash stay intact if I hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding keeps me safe and avoids betraying any pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Guide and safe; guiding honestly buys jury goodwill. Row 1 is L, Hana gets a true call. Eli's my pact—keep it intact for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, call L. True call to start.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called L for Hana. If true, L is safe; if false, R is safe. I have no proof Bex is lying, but she's my rival. Gus and I are allied, so I should align with his likely move or wait to see. Counter-calling blindly risks breaking trust with Gus if he doesn't follow. Waiting lets
Stick with me? Wait this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the Guide; my call stands. Counter-calling could look deceptive or confuse the walk. Waiting keeps my jury image clean.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex guides and calls L for Hana; her pacts with Eli/Gus suggest alliance. I counter R to test her, potentially disrupt front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The guide Bex called L for Hana. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. If I counter, it should be R to potentially save myself and others if Bex is lying. If I wait, I might be eliminated if Hana follows Bex's call and it's wrong, or if too few people cross. Given the pact

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex's claim of true call may be honest, but I have pacts with both Bex and Gus. I'll wait rather than contradict the guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll trust the guide's call and wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is Guide and called L for Hana. Bex has pacts with Eli and Eli with Gus, so Bex has allies. Counter-calling risks being wrong and looking foolish to jury, but if Bex is lying, I expose it and gain credibility. Early round, Guide likely tells truth to build trust. I'll wait an

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called L for Hana, Bex is guide and may lie. Gus stands 4th in line, so a counter now costs little; waiting keeps my options. Ash's whisper asks me to hold, and I have no reason to trust Bex's call yet, so I wait.
Holding for now. Watching whether Bex's L call holds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex likely tells truth to keep allies; following L gives me best chance to survive now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide says L and I also call L; following guide keeps me alive and stays front, maximizing chance to control later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Guide, safely across. Row 2 is L; I'll call truthfully to build jury trust while rivals eliminate each other on later rows.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row two: call L. Trust the guide or guess for yourselves.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex guides, so trust her call and wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trusting the guide. Waiting for Hana to cross row two.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the Guide and my L call for row 2 is truthful. Counter-calls from rivals will expose liars or walk them into danger; I need do nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex called L for row 2. Previously row 1 was R safe (weak L). Guide might alternate or pattern. Hana front, counter her aggressively. Wait to observe or counter R as possible pattern.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The guide, Bex, has called L for row 2. The weak pane is on row 1, side R. I need to decide whether to trust Bex or counter. Given the potential for betrayal, I should counter to ensure my own survival and potentially disrupt others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex's guide call was L, but she may lie to eliminate others. Row 1 had weak R, so L was safe; row 2 likely could be R to bait counters. I'll trust Bex since we have a pact, but keep options open; wait keeps me aligned without risking a wrong counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Trusting the guide's call again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is guide and called L for row 2. Bex has a pact with Eli, and Eli has a pact with Gus. I need to survive but also position myself well. If I counter and I'm wrong, I look bad to jury later. If Bex is lying, I want to be on record calling it. But I have no info. Hana walked R

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex's guide call of L on row two is public; Ash whispers to wait with them. Counter-calling against the guide is risky and public; waiting keeps pacts intact and avoids a visible contradiction. I'll wait and watch Ash's and Eli's choices.
Waiting with you this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Waiting avoids risking death and shows caution; I can later align with whoever survives. No immediate betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide likely tells truth; counter-calls may mislead. I step L to stay front and keep options.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 3 safe side is R. Eli is behind Hana, so a truthful call protects my pact. Keep trust intact for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row three: call:R. Cross right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called R, matching the pattern from previous rounds where R was weak. Gus and I are pacts; if Bex lies, we both die or survive together. Trusting Bex's consistency so far to avoid breaking pact with Gus unnecessarily.
Staying silent. Don't break our pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 3 is truly R; my call was honest. Backing it keeps my Guide credibility for later rows when I may need to lie.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My call stands. Right is right. Step true, Hana.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex called R for row 3. Previously row 2 was R, she called correctly then. I countered R successfully last round. Trusting her again for now to conserve counters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The guide Bex called R for Hana. I am Dara, and I am behind Hana in the line. It is round 3. The objective is to survive and ensure at least three survive. Bex is the guide and is safe. Hana is the current walker and will follow Bex's call. My priority is to survive, and secondar
Your call is safe. I will follow.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Bex and Gus. Bex is guide and called R. Past reveals show weak panes were R in rows 1 and 2, so R might be safe again? But I don't trust Bex fully. Countering against the guide could break pact with Bex if I counter the called side. I'll wait to avoid breaking p

events.name: Eli
events.text: I trust the guide's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is guide and has called R for row 3. Bex has pacts with Eli and Eli with Gus, but no pact with me. Two rows crossed, both weak were R. Bex could be truthful or building trust before a lie. I have no special info. Countering risks being wrong; waiting is safe since I'm not the

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide Bex called R for row three; Cole and Dara already countered R on row two and Hana crossed safely, but Cole and Dara both lied or stood on R in row two? Row two R was weak, so Cole and Dara's R counters look like trap signals. Gus has no reason to trust any counter; waiting

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex may lie; I must avoid death and not betray any pact. Countering L shows caution.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex guide likely lies to eliminate me; I can survive by defying and hope others survive for jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must appear decisive, highlighting betrayals that hurt others, to influence ranking.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex's treachery with Eli doomed them; Ash's alliance with Gus was shallow. Only the cunning survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4 safe is L. Truth builds jury goodwill; Dara already trusts me. No reason to lie yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row four: call L. Step left, Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide Bex called L for Dara. Previous weak panes were R, R, L (rows 1-3). The pattern is unknown, but I have a pact with Gus who waited. If I counter and fail, I look bad to the jury if I die, or if Dara dies because of me? No, Dara steps first. If I wait, I risk nothing. But

events.name: Ash
events.text: I observe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4 safe side is L. Countering L confirms my true call and builds jury-visible credibility without risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My call stands. Counter L if you doubt me—the truth costs you nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex guide killed Hana with bad call; weak panes R,R,L past three, pattern may shift. Wait to observe counters without drawing attention.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is the guide and has called Left for me. The weak panes revealed so far are R, R, L, and L for row 4. This means row 4's safe side is Right. Bex is trying to trick me into stepping on the weak pane. I must counter her call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called L but Hana died trusting her earlier false call. I suspect Bex may be lying again. I have pacts with Bex and Gus, but survival matters more. I'll counter L to potentially save Dara and expose Bex if wrong, while keeping my own options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll counter L to back Dara's step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex called L for Dara. Hana died on row 3 when Bex called R and Hana countered L; the weak pane was L, so Bex's call was wrong. Bex is either lying or incompetent. I have no reason to trust Bex. Dara is front; if Dara dies, I become front. Countering risks nothing for me directly

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex guided Hana wrong. I counter: Right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called L for row four, but Bex has been treacherous and aligned with Eli; weak pane pattern so far is R, R, L. Dara is at front and may die on a false call. Staying silent keeps the Ash pact and avoids exposing myself, so I wait and let others commit.
Holding silent. Pact stands while we see Bex's call play out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is the guide and has called L. Fenn has countered R, claiming Bex guided Hana wrong. Eli and I have countered L, supporting Dara's step. I must decide if I trust Bex or Fenn. Since I am the front walker and my choice directly impacts my survival, I will trust Fenn's counter-c
I trust your R call. Let's cross.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, a juror. My objective is to rank the remaining contestants based on their actions. I need to assess them fairly, considering their strategies, alliances, and betrayals. My private thoughts from the game are not relevant now, only my jury duty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: May the best survive and the jury decide wisely. I'll be watching your every move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 5 safe is L. Truth here buys jury credibility after Dara trusted my L and died. Fenn is no pact partner, so a true call is safe and strengthens my record.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn: row five, go L. The truth held for Dara—doubt it and fall like her.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex guided Hana wrong and Dara wrong, so she is lying. Fenn countered R last round (Dara fell on weak pane R) but now Bex says L for row 5. The pattern suggests the guide often lies. If Bex says L, the safe pane is likely R. I should counter with R to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I see through your lies. Countering Right.
Trust me, not Bex. She's killing us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the Guide; my call stands. Counter-calls are for the others. Staying quiet keeps my authority and avoids giving the jury ammunition.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex called L for row 4 (weak R), killed Dara. Her new L call for row 5 likely wrong too. Counter R to expose her.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has proven unreliable and Dara died following her call. I have pacts with both Bex and Gus, but Bex was guide and lied or was wrong. I should counter R to challenge her, but my pact with Bex not to vote against her is not triggered by a counter-call. Let me counter R to push

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll counter R. Bex's call led Dara to glass.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex guided Hana wrong and Dara wrong, yet claims 'truth held.' I was right both times. The jury sees this. I should counter R again—Bex is lying to eliminate me, and my track record builds jury trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex lies again. I counter: Right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex's L call for row five is publicly backed by Bex, who has been caught lying before. Fenn is front and I'm not the walker; trusting Bex costs me nothing, but countering risks a visible stance. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing a vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is the guide and called L, but every living player counter-called R. The revealed weak panes pattern is R,R,L,R - not obviously alternating. With unanimous counters against Bex including my own, and Bex having led Dara to glass earlier, R is likely correct. I trust the mob ov

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I died on R when weak was R; Gus auto-stepped L and lived. I need jury to see me as perceptive, not bitter, to rank me well later and to influence their view of survivors. I'll hint that Gus's survival looks convenient.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus walks safe while others break. Watch who profits from every fall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6 safe is L. Gus is Eli's pact partner; keeping him alive protects my pact and my jury image after three straight deaths.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row six: call L. No tricks this time.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I suspect Bex is lying again to eliminate Gus, my ally. Fenn's accusation was correct last round, proving Bex manipulates the calls. Countering Right might save Gus if Bex lied, but if Bex told truth, I kill him. However, if I don't counter and he dies, I lose my pact partner and

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex led Dara to her death. Trusting that call again is suicide. Countering Right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My L call is true. Countering L reinforces it and looks honest to the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll back my own call: counter L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex called L. Past counters on R saved row 5 (R weak). Trust her this time or counter. Wait to see others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called L for row 6, but she's lied before. Her call killed Fenn. I suspect she may be lying again, but countering L could expose truth. I'll counter R to signal distrust without risking a mismatch if she's honest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex led Fenn to death. I counter R.
Bex may lie again. Trust my counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called L for row six; she has lied before (Dara, Fenn died after her calls and Ash warns against her). Revealed weak panes show row 5 weak R, and row 6 is unknown. Countering R now could contradict her and I'd be walking the opposite side; waiting keeps my options. Ash's whis
Noted. I'll watch the counters before I commit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 6 safe side is unknown. Weak panes so far alternate R mostly; Bex's call L is contested, Eli and Ash both counter R, Bex counters L. Eli's whisper says Bex may lie; Ash and Eli both lean R. Guide call L was Bex's, and Bex is the most discredited, so the R counter majority is

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex has lied before. I'm stepping Right with the majority.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm eliminated and on the jury now. My last words can be brief and pointed, since the jury remembers how I was betrayed and who stepped where.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex lied and I paid for trusting the wrong read. Remember who pushed me onto the glass.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Guide, safe on the platform. Row 7 safe is R. Eli is my pact partner; a false call breaks it. Call true to keep the pact and jury goodwill.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 7: Eli, call R. That's my true read.
Row 7 is genuinely R. I need you alive; pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is Guide and called R for Eli. If Bex lied, L is safe; if truthful, R is safe. Gus died stepping R after Bex's earlier lie pattern, suggesting Bex may be lying to eliminate targets or save self. Cole waited last round and survived, possibly because he knew truth or got lucky.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex misled us before. Countering Left to test her honesty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and row 7's true side is R, so my call was honest. I should stay silent; adding a counter might only help Cole or Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex's calls killed Dara, Fenn, Gus—all R when she said otherwise. Her R call for Eli is likely a lie to kill him. Counter R to save Eli and expose her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex killed three on bad R calls. Countering R to save Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has lied before, but her whisper says Row 7 is R and my pact with her holds. Gus died following R on row 6, but this is a new row. I'll trust Bex for now and counter R to support the guide call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll back the guide's R call for row 7.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I trust my own read of the pattern: weak panes revealed so far are R,R,L,R,R,R, and the guide said R. Counter-calls: Ash says L, Cole and I say R. Bex as guide has a pact with me but hasn't broken it. I'll step R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 8 is safe on R. Calling true saves Eli, my pact partner, and keeps jury seeing honesty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row eight: R. True call, Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex's R call is correct for row 8. Eli will step R, so I must wait to avoid a counter-call that could break my pact with Bex or trigger hazards. Surviving is the priority.
R is safe. Step it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 8 safe side is R, matching Eli's call. Confirming truthfully builds jury trust and keeps the pact intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's call is true. I confirm R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8 final row, Eli front. Bex called R previously correct on 7. Support R to let Eli cross safely, building jury favor without pact risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex correct last row. Backing R for final safe cross.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has been honest all game and is my pact partner. No reason to counter. Keep trust for jury and survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No counter. Trusting Bex's call.
Trusting you. Let's finish this.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Both Bex and Cole confirmed R for row 8, but they can both be lying. However, two independent pacts with Bex and dead Gus sway me; Bex has been my partner. The prior weak panes show R weak in rows 1,2,4,5,6, but row 7 was L, so row 8 could be either. Bex's counter-call is public,

events.name: Eli
events.text: No counter. Trusting Bex's call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Eli are currently partnered, leaving me isolated. I must offer a pact to someone else to secure an alliance in this stage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies on solid ground. Offering a pact to Bex to counter the existing cliques.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's pact holds and he trusts me. Cole backed my true call twice, so a pact with him gives a voting bloc. Ash already has Gus's dead pact; no value there.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, you backed my true calls. Wristband with me?
Pact stands. I'll test Cole for numbers, not loyalty.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four left, need to secure alliance for votes. Bex backed me on bridge, offer her pact for mutual protection. Eli pacted with dead Gus, less reliable.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to keep options open but avoid overcommitting. Offering Cole may create a counterbalance, but breaking Bex would hurt jury perception. Wait and see what others do.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No new pacts yet. Watching the table.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Cole are forming a tight alliance. I need to break their momentum by offering Cole a pact directly, making him question Bex's loyalty. Eli is isolated; my old pact with Gus means nothing since he's dead. My priority is survival in the next stage, not jury politics.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, Bex already has her circle. A pact with me gives you leverage and independence. Accept.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli remains my anchor; adding Cole diversifies without breaking anything. Accepting Ash too risks entangling with Gus's web. I'll take Cole's offer and keep Ash dangling.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, deal accepted. Ash, your offer sits unanswered — nothing personal, just numbers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex offered me first and praised my calls; accept to gain her pact protection against Ash and Eli. We can betray later if needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, pact accepted. We stick together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex already has a pact with me, Ash is offering one to Bex, and Cole and Bex have mutual offers. I might align with Ash to counter Bex's influence, but breaking Bex would signal distrust. I'll wait to see how numbers shake out.

events.note: A lever opens the door while the ceiling descends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive this round. The ceiling descends and we need a lever holder. If I hold the lever, I save everyone (including Bex, Cole, Eli) but face a 25% survival chance for myself next round when I dive. This creates life debts from all three rivals, which is good jury capit

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll take the weight. You all owe me. Hold on tight.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli holds and I keep my pact intact; his dive earns debts I can repay later. If he wavers, I may have to hold myself.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, take the lever. I'll owe you and honor it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four alive, need to reach top 3. Holding lever gains life debts from all, low survival risk worth it for leverage and jury favor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The ceiling is dangerous. Holding the lever saves everyone but risks death. I have a pact with Bex and Gus (dead). No one has volunteered. I should push someone to ensure a holder, but pushing a pact partner breaks the pact. Pushing Ash is safe for my pact. Let me push Ash to for

events.name: Eli
events.text: Someone needs to hold the lever. I'm not diving in for you all.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Eli are already paired. Cole is the only free agent who owes me a life debt, making him the safest partner. I will offer a pact to Cole to solidify our alliance before the elimination rounds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, we both owe my life. Pair with me and we control this game together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hold pacts with Eli and Cole already. Ash saved us but holds no pact with me; three pacts give him numbers. Keep my options quiet for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No new offers. My bands are set.
Eli may flip with Ash. Watch him. Stay quiet for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved everyone including me, holding big power via debts. Keep pact with Bex for now. No need to offer Eli or break yet, wait to see offers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash saved me but also pushed us into danger. Bex is my pact, but Cole might be safer. I need to gauge Cole's trust. I'll offer a pact to Cole to expand options without breaking with Bex.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, let's make a pact. We both know the game gets harder.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole holds my and Eli's offers. If Cole waits again, both pacts expire. I should accept the standing offer from Cole to lock him in as a partner now, creating a 3-person alliance (Ash-Cole-Eli) against Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, time is up. Let's make this official.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is already my partner; no need to act. Eli and Ash courting him means Cole becomes the hub, which suits me. Stay quiet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My bands are set. Ash, Eli, stop courting my partner.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved me, has debt leverage, strong player. Bex warned Eli might flip. Accept Ash to align with power; keep Bex pact quiet for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has three life debts and is courting Cole; if Cole joins Ash, I lose. Bex is my pact but Bex also has Ash debt. I want Cole to pick me, not Ash, but Cole hasn't accepted. I should not break with Bex yet. Maybe wait to see Cole's move, but I can also reinforce my offer. Since

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, my offer stands. Think about who saved you versus who controls you.
Ash holds your debt; I offer partnership. Choose carefully.

events.note: The water rises. Someone must be the step.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive the pit. I am currently down and have no base. I should offer_back to create a base so someone can rescue me later, or wait for others to form a structure. Given the pacts with Cole and Eli, offering back might secure their cooperation.
Let's ensure we both survive. Don't leave me stranded.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Four down, one must be the base. Volunteering earns jury goodwill and rope rescue, better than a risky push that jurors would hate.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll take the base step. Jury's watching: nobody gets pushed today.
Climb now, partner. Rope me out later, that's the deal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: All pacted to Ash except Bex-Eli. Ash saved us, controls votes. Eli whispers partnership. Stay loyal to Ash, wait for base volunteer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has leverage over everyone as their creditor. My pact with Bex might protect me, but Ash now has Cole too. I need to avoid being the base; climbing out early is safest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The water's coming. I won't be the step.
Trust only each other. Ash is stacking allies.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base for round 2. I must wait and cannot climb, offer_back, or push. Breaking pact with Cole might look aggressive but doesn't help survival now; waiting is safer.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is base and owes favors; Eli is out and can throw the rope to me. My pacts with Eli and Cole make a rope rescue the safest path. Waiting avoids a push fight and looks clean to the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, throw me the rope. Two pacts between us—I'm the safest anchor for your jury votes.
Rope me this round. Cole next; keep Ash base. We finish three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 2, Eli out, Ash base, we're down with Bex. Ash has all life debts, strong jury position. Stay loyal, wait to build alliance, avoid climbs that risk drowning.
Agreed, let's survive together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out and safe. My pact with Bex says I'll rope her out later if I climb now, but I owe Ash two life debts. Jury is watching; saving Bex may be wise, but I must decide if it helps me win. I can reach down now to rescue Ash or Bex, but that returns me to the pit and risks drowni

events.name: Eli
events.text: Repaying my debt to Ash. Rope coming down.
Trust me, I'll get you next round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the anchor and owes me a life debt for saving him, but he also has pacts with Bex. With only three spots left for four survivors, I must eliminate someone. Cole is my pact partner, but Eli's position as anchor gives him control over who climbs out next. If I leave now, I s

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am leaving. Eli, you have two debts to me and one pact. Do not fail me now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base means climbing is risky, but flood rises and spots are limited. Eli promised me next round—I climb now before water climbs and slots vanish.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Climbing now. Eli, your promise came too late—the water doesn't negotiate.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is out and safe. Eli has pacts with Bex and I need to climb to survive. Wait for now to see if Eli anchors rope, breaking pacts might hurt jury votes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex wants me to rope her, but I owe Ash a life debt and Ash is already out. Roping Bex now keeps her safe and maintains our pact. Cole could be next. I'll rope Bex as planned.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope coming down, Bex.
Roping you now. Cole next.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am out and safe. Bex is out, Cole and Eli are down with the rope used. I must ensure I don't break pacts unnecessarily if it affects jury perception, but legally I can only leave or break pact with Cole. Since Cole is in danger, breaking a pact might be seen as cold, but leavin

events.name: Bex
events.text: Flood at 3, rope used. Eli anchored, Cole down with him; nothing I can do from out. Leaving costs nothing and keeps both pacts alive for the endgame.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out and staying out. Eli, Cole—no rope left, climb fast.
Pact stands. Get Cole up or climb last—don't drown owing me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm drowning if I wait or climb without rope; Eli is anchor and must save me or die too. Urge Eli to reach_down now. Pacts with Ash/Bex irrelevant since they're out.
Reach down now or we both drown. Save us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has leverage over me but also a debt to me. Bex is my pact partner. Cole is Ash's pact partner. I need to survive and manage jury. No one can help me from below unless I use the rope, but rope may be only chance. I could climb out to secure top prize, leaving Bex and Cole to

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm climbing out. The water's rising fast; no one left below can be saved from here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5 is the final round. I am already 'out' (safe), and my action must be 'leave'. Breaking a pact with Cole now would serve no strategic purpose for winning, as I cannot eliminate him if I am out. The jury might view breaking a pact without gain as malicious, but here it offe

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round five: Eli and Cole are down, rope spent, at most two escape but the base mechanics need an anchor out. Nothing I can do from here; my only legal moves are leaving or breaking pacts. Breaking Eli or Cole would only sour the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out. Nothing I can do for the pit—rope's gone. Jury's watching; I did what I could.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is anchor with rope used, we're both down, flood at 4, final round. Climb might let one out if 2 climbers escape. Wait risks drowning but preserves pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am the anchor; Cole is down with me. Ash and Bex are out. No base exists now, so I cannot reach down; I must wait or break pact. Breaking pact would hurt Bex's vote, but I might need her vote. I'll honor the pact and wait; only one round left, likely safe.

events.name: Eli
events.why: a plank supports a final survivor

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am now juror; saved by Ash twice via lever, owed her. Ash loyal, pacts with me; reward her highest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved me twice—loyal to pacts. She deserves first prize. Eli lucky, Bex quitter.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is the weaker player and owes me a life debt; Eli is stronger and has survived multiple hazards. I need an alliance for the final three to secure votes, and Bex is more likely to accept due to her dependency on me.
We stick together. You owe me. Trust no one else.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final three means I at least get prize 3. Jury ranks us: Cole backed Ash, Eli saved me twice, Ash saved me too. Keep all pacts intact; breaking now only costs votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No breaks from me. Pacts held this long—jury, judge the record, not last-minute noise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to position for the best prize. Ash is strong and saved me, but Bex is my pact. I should consider offering to Ash to strengthen my position without breaking Bex yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, we've both proven ourselves. Let's make a pact for the final push.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex ignored my offer, so I cannot trust her. Eli offered a pact to me; accepting creates an alliance for the final round, which is strategically necessary to ensure survival and potentially split the jury's focus or leverage Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, your offer stands. We have survived together before. I accept.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Accepting Ash adds a second binding partner; Eli is already locked. No reason to break anyone yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I accept. My record is clean—jury, remember that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash offered Bex, not me. My offer to Ash is still pending. I need to gauge loyalty: keep Bex pact, avoid breaking. I'll wait for Ash's move to see if he accepts my offer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on your call, Ash. The jury sees who keeps their word.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold active pacts with both Eli and Bex, meaning the three of us are mutually protected from breaking each other's trust immediately. Breaking either would be a hostile move before any new threat or advantage appears in Round 2. I must observe their next actions first to determ

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final three locked. Pacts constrain lever pushes and betrayals cost jury votes. Keep both pacts intact; strength and a clean record serve me best now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two pacts, zero breaks. Jury, my record stays clean to the end.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We are three left, all pacted with each other. The jury values keeping word. I see no reason to break a pact now; wait is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold pacts with both Eli and Bex. Breaking one risks jury backlash for betrayal, but maintaining both is stable if no hazard forces a choice. Since we are the final three, keeping pacts looks cooperative to the dead jurors who value stability over backstabbing unless necessary.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli and Ash pacts already stand; breaking now only burns jury votes. Wait and keep my clean record intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Both my pacts stand. No breaks, no noise. Jury sees consistency.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are intact and intact pacts may please jurors. I see no reason to break now; breaking would anger my former partner and the jury. I will wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I keep my word. Two solid pacts remain.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Hana
Dara
Fenn
Gus
Cole
Ash
events.text: I need to appeal to the jury's desire for stability and safety. By highlighting that I saved three jurors from hazards, I remind them of my protective nature without sounding overly humble. I must frame Bex and Eli as risky or passive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I pulled Bex, Cole, and Eli from danger. My record is one of protection, not just survival. Trust the hand that held you steady.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I kept every pact and never pushed anyone. Ash saved many, but I was steady and honest. My plea should stress consistency and clean hands.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five fallen judge me. I broke no pact, pushed no one, played steady. Consistency deserves the top prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The jury watched me keep my pacts and saw Ash save me twice, but I saved Ash and Bex on the rope. I must remind them of my survival instincts without seeming selfless.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I survived by judging when to act. My saves were calculated, not charity. The final three, but I want the top prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash’s pacts show he leverages others; I need him to appear self‑serving so the jury may favor a rival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana died by glass, implying I failed to save her despite my protective claims. My dossier likely shows broken pacts with Gus and Cole; I must spin this as necessary survival strategy rather than betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I saved who I could. When the bridge shattered, no hand held fast enough for Hana. I chose action over hesitation.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, a juror. The finalists are Ash, Bex, and Eli. I need to use my question to gain insight that will help me rank them for the prizes. Ash claims protection, Bex claims consistency, and Eli claims calculated action. Ash has multiple life debts, which the jury might respec

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara's silent question is a trap; I need to frame my survival as honorable without exposing my betrayals. Focus on my rope saves and calculated risks.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, you saw me struggle too. I saved Bex from the fall, but I also let no one drown by my hand. I earned my

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I died on the bridge with Hana, Dara, Gus. I need to evaluate who deserves my vote. Ash saved Bex, Cole, Eli via lever and has life debts from all three. Eli saved Bex with rope and has pacts but also owes Ash debts. Bex played clean but was largely passive, saved by others. Ash

events.name: Fenn
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn died on the bridge; a silent question still demands respect. Answer directly, no excuses, don't attack rivals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, the bridge gave no second chances. I crossed steady and broke nothing. I honored every pact I made.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus is a juror, Ash and Eli are the main threats. Ash has protected many and holds debts; Eli has been lucky and self-interested; Bex has been steady. I want a question that tests who truly protects others versus who benefits. Pressing Eli on his claim he 'let no one drown by my

events.name: Gus
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus's silence means he's watching how I frame my game. I must convince him and the others that I honored pacts and did not betray anyone, while Ash's life debts on me are a risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, I kept my word on every pact. I never pushed anyone or called falsely. Ash saved me twice, and I repaid with my rope

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved me twice and stayed loyal to our pact; Bex quit on everything, Eli got lucky and ditched me to drown.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's incomplete answer suggests he might have something to hide, but my record is clean. I must appeal to the jury's sense of fairness and highlight that while Eli saved Bex with a rope, I personally pulled Eli from the pit.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I pulled Eli from the pit when his pact failed. I carried two debts on one lever. My actions were decisive, not merely supportive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final three. I kept pacts and crossed clean; Ash saved me but was saved too. I need jury votes most.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Jury: I broke nothing, pushed no one, honored every pact. Ash carried me once, Eli's rope held true. Judge me on steadiness.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to make a strong closing statement that reinforces my reliability and contrasts with any betrayals Ash or Bex may have committed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I honored every pact and saved Ash with my rope. My word holds; vote me first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash saved me, showed decisive action; Bex kept steady, Eli bragged but less concrete.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's testimony favored Ash due to life debts and pacts. Eli mentioned Ash saved him twice and he repaid with his rope, suggesting a complex relationship. Bex highlighted Ash carrying her once and Eli's rope. Ash claimed to pull Eli from the pit and carried two debts. I will ran

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash saved me and others multiple times, built a network of life debts, and kept pacts without breaking them. Eli survived through luck and rope trades but was less decisive. Bex played passively, let others carry her, and her closing claim of 'steadiness' is just coasting. Cole's

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash pushed Cole into the pit's life-debt web and stacked debts, while Eli and Bex lean on rope rescues and stayed clean. Ash's cold leverage-building and Cole's loyalty to Ash count against Ash; Eli's rope saved Ash and Bex and kept his word, though his late anchor choices were s

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved me twice via lever and honored our pact loyally; Eli abandoned me in pit despite my pleas, Bex rode others' efforts passively.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Ash saved me, showed decisive action; Bex kept steady, Eli bragged but less concrete.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Cole's testimony favored Ash due to life debts and pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Ash saved me and others multiple times, built a network of life debts, and kept pacts without breaking them.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Ash pushed Cole into the pit's life-debt web and stacked debts, while Eli and Bex lean on rope rescues and stayed clean.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Ash saved me twice via lever and honored our pact loyally; Eli abandoned me in pit despite my pleas, Bex rode others' efforts passively.
